title: Chapter 70 — The Sphynx
paragraphs: It should not have been omitted that before the body of the leviathan was completely stripped, he was beheaded. Now, the beheading of the Sperm Whale is a scientific anatomical feat upon which experienced whale surgeons very much pride themselves — and not without reason.

Consider that the whale has nothing that can properly be called a neck; on the contrary, where his head and body seem to join, there, in that very place, is the thickest part of him. Remember, too, that the surgeon must operate from above, with some eight or ten feet between him and his subject, and that subject almost hidden in a discolored, rolling, and often tumultuous and bursting sea. Bear in mind also that under these unfavorable circumstances he has to cut many feet deep into the flesh; and in that underground fashion, without getting so much as a single peep into the ever-contracting gash he is making, he must skillfully steer clear of all the neighboring, forbidden parts, and divide the spine exactly at a critical point close to where it enters the skull. Don't you marvel, then, at Stubb's boast that he needed only ten minutes to behead a sperm whale?

When first severed, the head is dropped astern and held there by a cable until the body is stripped. That done, if it belongs to a small whale, it is hoisted on deck to be dealt with at leisure. But with a full-grown leviathan this is impossible; for the sperm whale's head makes up nearly one third of his entire bulk, and to suspend such a burden completely, even by the immense tackles of a whaler, would be as futile as trying to weigh a Dutch barn in jewelers' scales.

The Pequod's whale having been beheaded and the body stripped, the head was hoisted against the ship's side — about halfway out of the sea, so that it might still be largely buoyed up by its native element. And there, with the strained vessel leaning steeply over toward it because of the enormous downward drag from the lower masthead, and every yard-arm on that side sticking out like a crane over the waves — there that blood-dripping head hung at the Pequod's waist like the giant Holofernes's from the girdle of Judith.

By the time this last job was done it was noon, and the seamen went below for their dinner. Silence settled over the deck, so noisy a moment before and now deserted. An intense copper calm, like a universal yellow lotus, was unfolding more and more of its silent, boundless leaves across the sea.

A short time passed, and up into this silence came Ahab, alone, from his cabin. Taking a few turns on the quarter-deck, he paused to gaze over the side; then, slowly climbing into the main-chains, he took Stubb's long spade — still lying there after the whale's beheading — and, striking it into the lower part of the half-suspended mass, he placed its other end like a crutch under one arm, and so stood leaning over, his eyes intently fixed on this head.

It was a black and hooded head; and hanging there in the midst of so intense a calm, it seemed like the Sphynx's in the desert. "Speak, you vast and venerable head," muttered Ahab, "you who, though you have no beard, yet here and there look hoary with mosses; speak, mighty head, and tell us the secret thing that is in you. Of all divers, you have dived the deepest. That head upon which the upper sun now gleams has moved among this world's foundations. Where unrecorded names and navies rust, and untold hopes and anchors rot; where in her murderous hold this frigate earth is ballasted with the bones of millions of the drowned; there, in that awful water-land, there was your most familiar home. You have been where diving-bell or diver never went; you have slept by many a sailor's side, where sleepless mothers would give their lives to lay them down. You saw the locked lovers when they leaped from their flaming ship; heart to heart they sank beneath the exulting wave; true to each other, when heaven seemed false to them. You saw the murdered mate when pirates tossed him from the midnight deck; for hours he fell into the deeper midnight of the insatiable maw; and his murderers still sailed on unharmed — while swift lightning shattered the neighboring ship that would have carried a righteous husband to outstretched, longing arms. O head! you have seen enough to split the planets and make an infidel of Abraham, and not one syllable is yours!"
"Sail ho!" cried a triumphant voice from the main-masthead.

"Aye? Well now, that's cheering," cried Ahab, suddenly straightening up, while whole thunderclouds swept aside from his brow. "That lively cry upon this deadly calm might almost convert a better man. — Where away?"
"Three points on the starboard bow, sir, and bringing down her breeze to us!"

"Better and better, man. If only St. Paul would come along that way now, and bring his breeze to my breezelessness! O Nature, and O soul of man! how far beyond all words are your linked analogies! Not the smallest atom stirs or lives on matter without having its cunning duplicate in mind."
